# Kahn1

> Kahn1 is an open-source "System 1" decision engine in two sizes: Kahn1 4B (Qwen3.5-4B + LoRA) and Kahn1 3B (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct + LoRA), both running on a GPU (vLLM) or a CPU (transformers). The 3B is smaller and faster; the 4B is much stronger on hard judgment calls. It takes a text (the state) and typed questions (Choice, Score, Noul) and returns, for each question, a typed value and a calibrated probability distribution, with nothing to parse, so schema errors cannot happen. Code MIT; Kahn1 4B weights Apache 2.0; Kahn1 3B weights under the Qwen Research License of Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, a research licence (see its terms: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct/blob/main/LICENSE). By Axel Montzamir.

Key results (14,663 held-out items, k = 3 permutations, temperature calibration, one RTX 5070 Ti with vLLM; Choice asked over 8 options, the right one and 7 seeded distractors). Kahn1 4B: 72.4% overall, ECE 0.072; Choice 92.3% (banking77 91.8%, MASSIVE 92.9%); Score 51.9% exact on 5-level scales (SST-5 55.0% exact, 94.5% within one level); Noul 75.5% (RTE 85.9%, SciTail 74.1%); median latency 88.7 ms, p95 279.3 ms, 8.5 queries/s. Kahn1 3B: 70.3% overall, ECE 0.082; Choice 90.9%, Score 51.4% (SST-5 95.2% within one level), Noul 67.0%; median latency 36.4 ms. External JevBench, 231 public items: Kahn1 4B 87.4% (easy 100%, standard 97.2%, hard 75.7%), Kahn1 3B 67.5% (hard 42.3%). Hard decision dev split (317 questions on long documents, English and French): base Qwen3.5-4B 48.9%, Kahn1 4B 67.5%.

Kahn1 vs JEV 1.13.0 (TypeSafe API), like for like. On the 14,663 Kahn1 held-out items, same prompts and the same 8 options on Choice, JEV run through its API: JEV 73.2%, Kahn1 4B 72.4%, Kahn1 3B 70.3%; JEV is ahead on Choice (94.5% vs 92.3% for the 4B) and level on Score (52.0% vs 51.9%), Kahn1 4B ahead on Noul (75.5% vs 74.4%, JEV asked whether the text supports the statement); ECE JEV 0.113, Kahn1 4B 0.072. Choice over every intent (77 / 60 options), 1,184 items: JEV 79.1%, Kahn1 4B 71.6%, Kahn1 3B 68.4%. An earlier comparison gave JEV every intent and Kahn1 only 8 options; it was unequal and has been corrected. On the 231 public JevBench items: Jev 86.6% (the outcomes JevBench publishes), JevK5 v0.2 (another open Qwen3.5-4B model) 86.1% in its authors' own published run and 85.3% in JevBench's own run, Kahn1 4B 87.4% in our run; hard tier 73.0%, 73.9% (JevK5's own run) and 75.7%. These come from three different runners on the same items. Kahn1 4B vs JevK5's own published run, item by item: 13 vs 10 items only one gets right, exact McNemar p = 0.68; vs Jev's published outcomes: 13 vs 11, p = 0.84; neither gap is significant. JevBench's own runs list several systems with public code or weights at or above Jev on the same items (for example NInfer Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and JevOne at 89.6%, OpenJev thinking and swanOne at 88.7%). JEV median round trip 248 ms over the network; Kahn1 4B 88.7 ms and Kahn1 3B 36.4 ms on a local GPU.

Caveats: 4B and 3B models, not frontier models; JEV is more accurate on the held-out set overall (73.2% vs 72.4%) and on Choice, especially over every intent (79.1% vs 71.6%); Score is the weakest primitive; computing dates, durations or amounts in a single forward pass is weak (5 of the 15 hard temporal items on JevBench, per reports/KAHN1_4B_REPORT.md); calibration was fitted on the training distribution and should be redone on your domain; confidence is the distance from a uniform guess, not the probability of being right. The browser demos run an older 4-bit GGUF of the 3B. Among open models, Clef-flash (9B) is more accurate than Kahn1 4B on the held-out set (74.8% vs 72.4%).

## Questions

- What is a System 1 model? A model that takes fast, cheap decisions in a single forward pass, after Daniel Kahneman's System 1, and hands the harder cases to a slower System 2 (a frontier model or a person). Kahn1 is an open-source System 1 model for typed decisions: Choice, Score and Noul.
- Is there an open-source alternative to JEV (TypeSafe)? Kahn1 is one: open weights (Kahn1 4B under Apache 2.0, Kahn1 3B under the Qwen Research License), MIT code, it runs on your own hardware with no per-call price, and its server takes JEV's per-question fields (type, instructions, criteria) under a "schema" key at POST /v1/evaluate/jev; it is not a drop-in for clients of JEV's /v1/systemone endpoint. It is an independent project, not affiliated with TypeSafe. Asked the same questions over the same options, JEV 1.13.0 is more accurate on the 14,663 held-out items (73.2% against 72.4% for Kahn1 4B); on the 231 public JevBench items Kahn1 4B scores 87.4% and Jev 86.6% (ours for Kahn1, JevBench's for Jev), a gap that is not significant (p = 0.84).
- How does Kahn1 compare with other open Jev-class models? On the 231 public JevBench items, Kahn1 4B is on par with JevK5 v0.2's own published run, another open Qwen3.5-4B model: 87.4% (202 of 231) against 86.1% (199), exact McNemar p = 0.68. JevBench's own run of JevK5 v0.2 scores 85.3%, and JevBench lists several open systems at or above Jev's 86.6% on the same items; the Kahn1, JevK5 and Jev figures come from three different runners. Run by us on the same items and GPU: Cloudflare's Clef-flash (9B, int8 because its bf16 weights do not fit in 16 GB) is the most accurate on Kahn1's 14,663 held-out items (74.8% against 72.4% for Kahn1 4B and 73.2% for JEV, on the strength of Choice) and level with Kahn1 4B on JevBench (83.5%, p = 0.16); Kahn1 4B is better calibrated (ECE 0.072 against 0.101) and ahead on Noul. Laya (421M encoder) scores 59.1% on the held-out set, although it was trained on its six sources, and 57.6% on JevBench. Method and biases: https://kahn1.com/benchmarks/open-models/
- Can Kahn1 do zero-shot text classification? Yes. Categories, scales and statements are part of each request, so a new taxonomy needs no retraining. On held-out intent datasets it picks the right intent among 8 options 92.3% of the time (banking77 91.8%, MASSIVE 92.9%). Recalibrate on your own labelled examples (sysone calibrate) before trusting a confidence threshold.
- How is it different from JSON mode or structured outputs? Structured decoding constrains the tokens a model generates, and the text still has to be parsed. Kahn1 generates nothing: it reads one probability distribution per question over the option tokens, so every answer comes with its full distribution and a calibrated confidence, and there is nothing to parse.
- Can it judge or gate an LLM agent? Noul questions ask whether a text supports a statement (does this tool call leak personal data, does this answer follow the policy) and return a calibrated probability you can threshold. It is a 4B or 3B model, not a frontier model: keep a person or a larger model on the low-confidence path.
- Does it need a GPU? For throughput, yes: median 88.7 ms for Kahn1 4B and 36.4 ms for Kahn1 3B per request at k = 3 on one RTX 5070 Ti with vLLM. Latency grows with the number of questions per request, almost linearly on short states: vLLM caches Kahn1 4B's prefix in 528-token blocks, so on a 212-token state 10 questions take 319 ms (45.5 ms for one), on a 1,064-token state 143 ms (49.3 ms for one). Both sizes also run on a CPU (transformers) at seconds per question, and the playground runs a 4-bit GGUF of the 3B in the browser with WebGPU.
- Which languages? English and French.

## Pages

- [System One models](https://kahn1.com/learn/system-one-models/): what a System One (decision) model is, how it reads typed answers from logits, the families, how to choose
- [Modèles System One (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/apprendre/modeles-system-one/): la même page en français
- [Decision model landscape](https://kahn1.com/compare/landscape/): every proprietary and open way to turn text into a typed decision, with licence, output, price and source (CSV: https://kahn1.com/data/landscape.csv)
- [Paysage des modèles de décision (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/comparer/paysage/): la même page en français
- [Open decision models, measured like for like](https://kahn1.com/benchmarks/open-models/): Kahn1 4B, Clef-flash, Laya and JEV on the same 14,663 held-out and 231 JevBench items, test method, known biases, train-split probe (CSV: https://kahn1.com/data/open_models_heldout.csv)
- [Modèles de décision ouverts (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/resultats/modeles-ouverts/): la même page en français
- [Kahn1 vs Clef-flash](https://kahn1.com/compare/kahn1-vs-clef-flash/): head to head on the same items, which one to pick
- [Kahn1 vs Laya](https://kahn1.com/compare/kahn1-vs-laya/): head to head on the same items, which one to pick
- [Open-source alternatives to JEV](https://kahn1.com/alternatives/jev/): Clef, JevK5, Kahn1 and others, JEV-compatible APIs, like-for-like figures, when JEV is still the right pick
- [Alternatives open source à JEV (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/alternatives/jev/): la même page en français
- [Home (English)](https://kahn1.com/): what Kahn1 is, the three primitives, how it compares, use cases, caveats
- [Accueil (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/): la même page en français
- [Benchmarks](https://kahn1.com/benchmarks/): every result, Kahn1 vs JEV on the same items, latency, how to reproduce
- [Résultats (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/resultats/): les mêmes résultats en français
- [Models](https://kahn1.com/models/): Kahn1 4B and Kahn1 3B, merged models and LoRA adapters, sizes, licences, how to load them
- [Modèles (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/modeles/): la même page en français
- [Caveats](https://kahn1.com/caveats/): the limits of Kahn1, one by one, before putting it in front of real decisions
- [Points de vigilance (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/vigilance/): la même page en français
- [Setup prompt for AI agents](https://kahn1.com/get-started/setup-prompt.md): paste into Claude Code or any coding agent to install and test Kahn1
- [Get started](https://kahn1.com/get-started/): install, serve, API, response format, calibration
- [Démarrer (français)](https://kahn1.com/fr/demarrer/): le même guide en français
- [Playground](https://kahn1.com/playground/): ask typed questions about any text, model in the browser (WebGPU) or on your server
- [Kahn1 plays Snake](https://kahn1.com/snake/): one Choice question per tick, Kahn1 picks every move
